# Summary

Anthropic's new life sciences research group used Claude AI to autonomously discover a novel enzyme system called array-associated reverse transcriptases (ARTs) with CRISPR-like properties by searching through massive DNA sequence databases. After 21 hours of analysis across roughly 950 Claude agents, the system identified repeating DNA patterns associated with reverse transcriptase genes in bacteriophages—a discovery validated by CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang as potentially significant for gene editing and other DNA manipulation applications. The finding demonstrates how AI can systematize and accelerate biological discovery when collaborating with human scientists in research workflows.
